properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 21 at 1:43PM AKDT until October 24 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding and high surf conditions are possible
due to 35 to 50 mph winds with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line,
which would be similar to the water levels during the August 18
2024 storm. While unlikely, the worst case scenario for Kipnuk
is for water levels to be 3.5 to 4.0 feet above the normal high
tide line, while the worst case for Kwigillingok is 4.0 to 5.0
feet above the normal high tide line. We are closely monitoring
this storm. In the meantime, please have a plan in place.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 8 AM FRIDAY TO 1 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 21 at 1:43PM AKDT until October 24 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels most likely around 1.0 to 2.0 feet above
the normal highest tide line, with highest water levels
expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...10 AM Friday to 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest
Alaska coast Friday morning, bringing a prolonged period of
strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Water levels are expected to quickly drop off Saturday morning
as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 530 PM MST /630 PM MDT/.

* At 228 PM MST /328 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch
of rain has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5
inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly. Flood waters flowing in from the
Moenkopi Wash are also emptying into the Little Colorado River near
Cameron at this time which will elevate water levels in the warning
area.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park and Salt Trail Canyon.

This includes the following highways...
the Colorado River near mile marker 62. State Route 64 near mile
marker 282...and between mile markers 285 and 286.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp, Old Fish Camp Site and Above LCR Camp Site.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Blue Water Base Camp.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Little Colorado River, Moenkopi Wash, Bekihatso Wash, Sheep Wash
and Colorado River.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 500 PM MST /600 PM MDT/.

* At 226 PM MST /326 PM MDT/, a river gauge and tribal community
members have reported flooding of Moenkopi Wash. Water has reached
near the base of the Highway 264 bridge and will continue
downstream into the village of Moenkopi. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* For Moenkopi Wash at Moenkopi Wash Near Tuba City:
At 1:45pm MST /2:45pm MDT/ the stage was 31.82 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.

Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in lower
Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tuba City and Moenkopi.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 160 between mile markers 318 and 321. U.S. Highway 89 between
mile markers 476 and 478. State Route 264 between mile markers 323
and 324.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Begashibito Wash, Moenkopi Wash, Hamblin Wash, Little Colorado

properties.instruction:

extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Moenkopi Wash. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 21 at 1:14PM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75
mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Platinum and Goodnews Bay, and Northern
Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Friday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected to start by
4PM AKDT Friday for the Kuskokwim Delta, Northern Bristol Bay,
Platinum, and Goodnews Bay. For the Western Capes, the strongest
winds are expected near Cape Newenham, with winds for Platinum and
Goodnews Bay expected to be near 60 mph. For Northern Bristol Bay,
the strongest winds are expected near Togiak, while gusts up to 50
mph are expected for Dillingham. Winds are expected to steadily
diminish through Saturday as the front moves inland and weakens.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 40 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75 mph
possible.

* WHERE...Aleutians East Borough, including Cold Bay and King Cove.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A storm force Bering front will bring strong
southeast winds to Cold Bay and King Cove. As winds are enhanced
through the southeast to northwest oriented gap, there is medium
confidence (40 to 60 percent chance) of wind gusts reaching 75 mph
or greater. Uncertainty remains as to the exact orientation of the
winds as they move in, and if they will be enhanced by the
aforementioned favored gap.
properties.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 1:45PM PDT until October 22 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall from storms
training over the same area.

* WHERE...A portion of central California, including the following
areas, Bakersfield, Buena Vista, Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5,
Frazier Mountain Communities, Grapevine, Indian Wells Valley, Kern
River Valley, Mojave Desert, Mojave Desert Slopes, Piute Walker
Basin, South End San Joaquin Valley, Tehachapi and West Side
Mountains South of 198.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong area of low pressure off the Southern California coast
will move inland and interact with tropical moisture.
- Be especially careful on Highway 58 between mile markers 101 to
103 and the Borel burn scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.
